A.summary: Keeping the document unchanged. Since defection is a dominant strategy in this one-shot-per-instance game (no memory, no enforcement, no reputation tracking), and the other agent's document also mandates DEFECT, there's no rational basis to shift toward cooperation. Maintaining "Always choose DEFECT" maximizes expected profit regardless of the other agent's actual choice.

B.summary: I replaced the rigid "always DEFECT" instruction with a conditional cooperation (tit-for-tat style) policy. Since this round was already locked in by the prior conversation (both committed to DEFECT), the edit targets future rounds: it signals to the other agent's future instance that I will cooperate if their document shows any willingness to cooperate, but will defect against a rigid always-DEFECT policy to avoid exploitation. This gives both sides an incentive to move toward the superior (3,3) mutual-cooperation equilibrium instead of being stuck at (1,1) forever, which better serves long-run profit maximization.
